claims.text: Intermediate thermal aging causes a transient ductile-brittle-ductile transition in FCC/B2 eutectic HEAs.
The transition is driven by precipitation of coherent ordered L1_2 or D0_3 nanoclusters within the B2 phase.
The ordered nanoclusters are potent, non-dissociable obstacles to dislocation glide.
Dislocation obstruction by the ordered clusters temporarily locks plasticity and sharply reduces ductility.
The clusters dissolve at higher temperatures, restoring ductility.
The initial alloy has a lamellar or rod-like microstructure containing a ductile FCC matrix and a hard ordered B2 phase.
The initial alloy contains no significant grain-boundary segregation.
Aging at approximately 400–600 °C permits diffusion and nucleation of ordered clusters without grain coarsening or phase decomposition.
A transient percolating network of coherent, compositionally modulated L1_2 or D0_3 precursors forms within B2 and at FCC/B2 phase boundaries.
The ordered-cluster network increases the critical resolved shear stress for dislocation entry into B2.
Ordered clusters generate local lattice-strain fields and increase the antiphase-boundary energy barrier for dislocation cross-slip and entry.
Dislocations cannot cut through the ordered domains without high applied stress.
Restricted dislocation cutting through ordered domains leads to brittle fracture.
Prior HEA evidence shows that an FCC alloy containing L1_2 ordered precipitates can be strengthened by the precipitates' high antiphase-boundary energy.
The minimum in tensile elongation should coincide with maxima in yield strength and ordered-cluster density.
The ordered-cluster density can be tracked through diffuse-scattering intensity.
The embrittlement regime is bounded by the temperature range in which the short-range-order parameter is maximized while thermal disordering remains insufficient.
Grain growth dominates above 1000 °C, whereas impurity segregation dominates below 300 °C.

contradictions.description: The intervention and conditions state that aging is insufficient for phase decomposition or phase separation, while the hypothesis proposes precipitation of structurally distinct L1_2 or D0_3 clusters from B2. The text does not clarify whether these are merely continuous local-order fluctuations or a true precipitate phase, leaving an internal tension.
